title: rorca-production-ready

userStories.title: GitHub Actions CI Pipeline
userStories.description: As a contributor, I want automated CI checks on every PR so regressions are caught before merge and the main branch stays green.
acceptanceCriteria: .github/workflows/ci.yml created with workflow name 'CI'
Triggers on: push to main, pull_request to main

Jobs run in parallel: frontend-typecheck (npx tsc --noEmit), backend-typecheck (cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit), backend-tests (cd backend && npm test), frontend-lint (npm run lint), frontend-tests (npx vitest run)
All jobs use Node 20 on ubuntu-latest
node_modules cached using actions/cache with hash of package-lock.json for both root and backend
Each job has a descriptive name visible in GitHub PR checks UI
README.md gets CI status badge: [![CI](https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](link)
Workflow file is valid YAML (no syntax errors) and uses actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4

userStories.title: Docker Image & docker-compose
userStories.description: As a self-hoster, I want to run Rorca with a single docker compose up command so setup takes under 5 minutes with zero Node.js knowledge required.
acceptanceCriteria: Dockerfile at repo root: multi-stage build with node:20-alpine as builder and runner stages
Builder stage: installs all deps, runs npm run build (frontend), copies backend with production deps only
Runner stage: copies built frontend dist to a directory Express can serve, sets RORCA_SERVE_STATIC=1 and RORCA_STATIC_DIR=/app/dist
Express serves frontend static files and SPA fallback in production mode
docker-compose.yml at repo root with: rorca service mapping port 3030:3030, named volume 'rorca-data' mounted at /app/backend for SQLite persistence, RORCA_TELEMETRY=0 as default env var
.dockerignore excludes: node_modules, .git, backend/rorca.db, *.env, .env.*, forge/specs/logs/
docker build -t rorca . completes without error on clean checkout
docker run -p 3030:3030 rorca + GET http://localhost:3030/api/health returns 200 with valid JSON
Image size under 500MB (verified with docker images rorca)

userStories.title: rorca CLI — start and init commands
userStories.description: As a developer installing Rorca globally, I want npm i -g rorca && rorca start to work so I can get started without reading docs.
acceptanceCriteria: bin/rorca.ts created as CLI entry point using commander.js or minimist for arg parsing
package.json bin field set to { "rorca": "./bin/rorca.js" }

rorca start: starts Express backend on port 3030 with RORCA_SERVE_STATIC=1, opens http://localhost:3030 in default browser using 'open' package, prints 'Rorca running at http://localhost:3030' to stdout

rorca init: detects if claude binary exists in PATH, runs 'claude mcp add --global rorca --transport http http://localhost:3030/mcp' if found, prints manual instructions if claude not found, handles already-registered case gracefully (no error on duplicate)
rorca --version prints version from package.json
rorca --help prints usage with available commands: start, init, --version, --help
bin/rorca.ts compiles via TypeScript with no errors
bin entry is included in npm package files array

userStories.title: Telemetry Opt-In & Privacy
userStories.description: As a privacy-conscious user, I want telemetry to be opt-in only (never default-on) and clearly documented, so I trust Rorca with my data.
acceptanceCriteria: RORCA_TELEMETRY env var controls telemetry: '0' or 'false' = off (default), '1' or 'true' = on
Telemetry is OFF by default — no data sent unless user explicitly opts in
When telemetry is on, only anonymous usage metrics are sent: event type (spec_generated, run_completed), agent type, story count, duration. NEVER: spec content, file paths, workspace names, API keys
PRIVACY.md file at repo root documents: what data is collected, when telemetry is on vs off, how to opt out, data retention policy
Settings panel gets a telemetry toggle in the Account tab with clear description: 'Help improve Rorca by sending anonymous usage statistics. No spec content, code, or file paths are ever sent.'
Health endpoint includes 'telemetryEnabled: boolean' field
Docker compose sets RORCA_TELEMETRY=0 by default

userStories.title: Helmet + Security Headers
userStories.description: As a security-conscious user, I want all standard HTTP security headers present on every response so common web vulnerabilities (clickjacking, MIME sniffing, XSS) are mitigated by default.
acceptanceCriteria: helmet npm package installed as production dependency in backend/package.json
app.use(helmet()) added early in middleware chain in backend/src/server.ts (before route mounting)

Content-Security-Policy header present on all responses — default-src 'self', script-src 'self', style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' (needed for Tailwind), img-src 'self' data: https:, connect-src 'self' ws: wss:
X-Frame-Options: DENY header present (prevents clickjacking)
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header present
Strict-Transport-Security header present with max-age=31536000
X-XSS-Protection: 0 header present (modern browsers, CSP is the real protection)
Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin header present
Permissions-Policy header restricts camera, microphone, geolocation to none
curl -I http://localhost:3030 shows all security headers
Existing CORS configuration is preserved (not broken by helmet)
SSE endpoints (/api/pipeline/stream, /api/pipeline/runs/:id/output) still work after helmet
Backend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Webhook Signature Verification Audit
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want all incoming webhook endpoints to verify signatures so forged webhook payloads are rejected.
acceptanceCriteria: GitHub webhook handler (webhook-handlers.ts) verifies X-Hub-Signature-256 header using HMAC-SHA256 with configured webhook secret
Missing or invalid signature returns 401 with { error: 'Invalid webhook signature' }
Pipeline hooks (pipeline_hooks table) that fire outbound webhooks include an X-Rorca-Signature header computed from HMAC-SHA256 of the payload body
Webhook secret is stored in vault_keys table (encrypted AES-256-GCM), not as plaintext env var
If no webhook secret is configured, inbound webhooks are rejected with 403 { error: 'Webhook secret not configured' } rather than accepted unverified
Timing-safe comparison used for signature verification (crypto.timingSafeEqual)

userStories.title: Memory Rotation & Archival Policy

acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/lib/memory-rotation.ts created with: rotateMemory(config) that moves old entries from active MEMORY.md to archive
Rotation policy: entries older than 30 days (configurable via MEMORY_RETENTION_DAYS env var) are moved to .rorca/memory/MEMORY_ARCHIVE.md
Exception: entries tagged with 'Architecture' or 'Convention' category are never rotated (they're permanent project knowledge)
Rotation preserves entry format — archived entries are valid MEMORY.md entries, just in a separate file
Active MEMORY.md capped at 200 entries max (configurable via MEMORY_MAX_ENTRIES). When exceeded, oldest non-Architecture/Convention entries rotate
Token budget: active MEMORY.md target < 8000 tokens. Rotation triggers when estimated tokens exceed this
POST /api/memory/rotate endpoint triggers manual rotation, returns { archived: number, remaining: number, tokens: number }
Rotation runs automatically after each pipeline run completion (via scheduler or post-run hook)

userStories.title: Spec Sanitizer — PII Scrubbing
userStories.description: As a user publishing a spec to the community marketplace, I want PII and secrets automatically scrubbed so I don't accidentally expose sensitive information.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/lib/spec-sanitizer.ts created with sanitizeSpec(specJson) function

8 regex patterns detect and redact: API keys (sk-, pk-, key_, Bearer patterns), email addresses, IP addresses, home directory paths (/Users/*, /home/*), AWS credentials (AKIA*), GitHub tokens (ghp_*, gho_*), URLs with authentication (https://user:pass@), custom secrets matching process.env.* references
Redacted values replaced with '[REDACTED]' — not deleted, so the spec structure is preserved
sanitizeSpec returns { sanitized: JSON, redactionCount: number, redactions: Array<{ field, pattern, original_preview }> }
original_preview shows first 4 and last 4 characters only: 'sk-a...xyz1' — enough to identify but not expose
Sanitizer works recursively on nested objects (story descriptions, acceptance criteria arrays)
POST /api/marketplace/preview-sanitize accepts spec JSON, returns sanitized version + redaction report (for the publish modal preview)
Unit tests cover all 8 patterns with real-world examples
Backend TypeScript compiles with no errors
